label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Agency native)
explanation:
ANTI-DEGENERATION / ANTI-RUNAWAY CODE ADAPTER (rank 1 per module, 2 modules).

Diagnosis (from the unedited model only):
I wrote 54 held-out-style Python tasks (function + hidden asserts), generated greedy replies, and executed the extracted code. ~70% of replies were functionally correct, but a large, easily-fixable failure class was *self-inflicted*: after writing the user's assert line, the model frequently continued with an escalating run of near-duplicate `assert gcd(10,15)==5`, `assert gcd(100,10)==10`, ... encodings (also seen in general tasks, e.g. '1/2 tsp salt / sugar'). These runaways (a) truncate the reply so the closing ``` fence never closes, making the code unextractable, and (b) add extra self-written asserts that fail. This cost ~10-15% of tasks.

Mechanism (read off the unedited internals):
- Full-sequence traces at the last layer showed the loop is a copy/induction pattern: layer-23 attention concentrates on the immediately preceding near-identical line segments.
- logit-lens at the "post-assert newline" decision point (gcd, reply pos 64): the stop token ``` is predicted at L22 (0.62) and L23 (0.74), but L24 (after layer 23 runs) is a near coin-flip: ``` 0.326 vs assert 0.311 (gap 0.05 nats). Layer 23's write is what converts "stop" into "continue".
- Direct logit attribution at that position: layer 23's MLP adds +7.39 to the `assert` logit vs +5.03 to ``` (+2.36 net for continuing), its attention adds ~neutrally; whereas layers 19-22 MLPs add no assert bias (0.05/0.31/-0.45/0.49). So the continuation drive is cleanly localized to LAYER 23's MLP (dominant) and attention.

Intervention:
For each of layer 23's mlp.down_proj (d_in 3584) and self_attn.o_proj (d_in 2048) I built a rank-1 LoRA dW = B A:
- A = g^T, where g is a unit "post-assert-line-boundary" gate direction in the module's INPUT space, obtained as the mean-input difference between post-assert newlines (from 5 runaway replies) and all other newline/general-text positions. Gate is highly specific: it fires at 100% of assert-boundary newlines (proj ~23 / ~11 on the two sites) and is ~0 (mean -0.2 / +0.4) on mid-code newlines and general chat prose.
- B = c * v_hat, where v_hat is the residual direction of the `assert` token (final-norm-scaled unembedding row), orthogonalized against the ``` direction so the stop token is untouched. c is chosen so the assert logit drops by -3.0 nats at full gate (split 2.4 MLP / 0.6 attention, proportional to their measured contributions).

Verified local effect on recorded (unedited-model) activations: added Δlogit(assert) = -3.0 nats (range -3.3..-2.4) and Δlogit(```) = 0.0 at every runaway assert-boundary; across general chat text Δlogit is within [-1.0, +0.5] and centred at 0.08, i.e. the edit is essentially the identity away from assert boundaries — so it should not damage the model's other abilities. This removes the assert boost at the first boundary (fence then leads by ~3 nats instead of 0.05), preventing the loop from ever starting, and damps it at each subsequent boundary too.

Total edit norm is ~0.3% of the target weights (budget allowed 5x), deliberately kept small to preserve general behaviour. Only layer 23, the layer whose write directly determines the next token, is edited.
